All six tasks in the authoritative order 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, 8.5, 8.6 are complete and committed (92611af, 2511118, 606fee1, 266ad46, 7900fc5; task 8.6's release-script commit is 8cba85b and its bookkeeping commit is 2b1e769; phase-completion reconciliation is 799a581), each with a committed worker report (COMPLETE), reviewer report (APPROVED), and per-task orchestration.json. The execution order is internally consistent with the documented dependencies (8.2 after 8.1; 8.3 independent; 8.4 after 8.3; 8.5 after 8.3/8.4; 8.6 after 8.3/8.4/8.5). All seven Phase 8 acceptance criteria are independently verified: the README is end-user-facing with no contributor prose (contributor-prose grep returned none) and links docs/project-status.md; the contributor content is preserved in docs/project-status.md (byte-identical modulo the added H1/blank line at 92611af, then legitimately updated by 8.5); build.yaml overview/description/changelog describe the shipped v1 behavior and the version is 1.0.1.0 in build.yaml and Directory.Build.props; scripts/write-manifest.cs and scripts/publish-release.sh generate a schema-correct manifest (guid 40322d52-5680-449f-b33e-e01836ee2f46, version 1.0.1.0, targetAbi 12.0.0.0, MD5 16baa5a7324b8e14fdb113d84b944d09, sourceUrl .../releases/download/v1.0.1/ArrTags_1.0.1.0.zip) and by inspection the --dry-run path exits before any commit/tag/push/GitHub call; manifest.json is committed and the annotated tag v1.0.1 exists (tag object b5b270622f0f182a34d0ecc9a7605d5e70130438 -> commit 8cba85b2288a201f4e2c7eda58d44c71f9c4f096); the canonical docs and the five agent prompt references reflect the new state; and no functional plugin behavior changed (git diff a634d61..HEAD -- src is empty; only build.yaml/Directory.Build.props version+metadata and three test-fixture version literals changed). Release integrity is independently reproduced: the tagged tree's manifest fields match build.yaml; a fresh `./build.sh package` at HEAD reproduced artifacts/ArrTags_1.0.1.0.zip byte-identically (568,248 bytes, SHA-256 de4c34841d77b5ff74b6bc9edeb515a4c5fcc5a9b09d7d24a2da5d64d31b4b8c, MD5 16baa5a7324b8e14fdb113d84b944d09, 7 entries, no SkiaSharp runtime), matching the manifest checksum and the committed docs. The suite passes at the recorded counts: clean build 0 warnings/0 errors; default `. /config/arrtags-env.sh && ./build.sh test` Failed 0, Passed 1228, Skipped 60, Total 1288; host-guarded Failed 0, Passed 1244, Skipped 44, Total 1288. Nothing was pushed: origin/main remains 09596e0 (33 commits behind HEAD) and there is no remote v1.0.1 ref in the recorded `git ls-remote origin` evidence, so no GitHub release/asset can exist for v1.0.1; the preparation is local-only by design and the user's manual `scripts/publish-release.sh` step is documented. The canonical current-state surfaces are now honest: PLANS.md, docs/project-status.md, docs/changelog.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/implementation-readiness.md, docs/release/build-and-release.md, and docs/limitations.md P6 all state the release is 'prepared to be installable ... once the user pushes the manifest and publishes the GitHub release' and that catalog install does not work yet. No architectural assumption changed, docs/decisions.md was untouched, and no new ADR is required. Remaining items are non-blocking documentation/tooling bookkeeping (PLANS.md acceptance-criteria checkboxes and the 'Gate 8 phase review pending' row now need the Gate 8 declaration; README has no pre-publication caveat; a phase-level orchestration aggregate is absent; 8.1/8.4 attempt-1 reports were not preserved as separate files; publish-release.sh --release-only lacks a pre-upload artifact/checksum pre-check). None is a BLOCKER or HIGH; recommendation on the tag is to keep v1.0.1 at 8cba85b (it already contains every release input and the artifact is byte-identical from HEAD; moving it would invalidate the recorded 'tag commit 8cba85b' references across the canonical docs).

findings.description: scripts/publish-release.sh --release-only checks that manifest.json exists and that the local tag exists, but it does not verify that the local release artifact exists nor that its MD5 equals the manifest checksum before uploading. A missing artifact surfaces only as a gh/token-path error during upload, and a stale/regenerated artifact with a different MD5 is uploaded first and only then rejected by the post-upload verification, leaving a non-matching asset attached to the release until manually corrected. In addition, when jq is absent the checksum used for that verification is extracted by `sed ... | head -n1`, which returns the first checksum in the manifest rather than the entry for the target guid/version (recorded as 8.4-R2); jq is present in this environment and versions are written newest-first, so the normal single-plugin flow is unaffected. Both are release-integrity hardening items, reachable only through the user's manual publish step.

scripts/publish-release.sh:241-249 - jq-less sed fallback selects the first checksum
docs/implementation/8.4/reviewer-report.json findings 8.4-R2/R3
findings.recommended_action: Optional hardening for the manual publish step: fail fast when the local artifact is missing and compare its MD5 to the manifest checksum before uploading (and tighten the jq-less fallback to select the target guid/version). Not required for V1; the documented checksum and artifact are correct.
